scenarios.title: Ad Stack Waterfall Performance Analysis
scenarios.description: Analyzing ad stack performance to optimize demand partner sequence and timeout settings
scenarios.query: Our current ad stack has Google Ad Manager as primary, followed by StreamVault Media Publisher Services, then Prebid with 8 demand partners. We're seeing 2.3 second average response times and 78% fill rate. Google fills 45% at $8.50 average CPM, StreamVault Media fills 25% at $6.20 CPM, and Prebid fills remaining 30% at $4.80 CPM. Should we reorder our waterfall or adjust timeout settings? Our page load speed target is under 2 seconds and we need to maintain revenue above $35,000 monthly.

scenarios.title: Audience Segmentation Revenue Impact
scenarios.description: Evaluating revenue impact of implementing granular audience segmentation for floor pricing
scenarios.query: We want to implement audience-based floor pricing across our 500K monthly users. Current data shows: returning users (60% of traffic) have 12% higher CTR, mobile users (70% of traffic) have $2 lower average CPM, users from tier-1 cities (40% of traffic) generate 35% more revenue per session. How should we segment our audience for dynamic floor pricing? What floor price adjustments would you recommend for each segment to maximize overall yield while maintaining 80%+ fill rates?

scenarios.title: Ad Placement Layout Revenue Optimization
scenarios.description: Optimizing ad placement positions and sizes to maximize viewability and revenue
scenarios.query: Our current layout has: header banner (728x90) with 95% viewability earning $15 CPM, sidebar banner (300x250) with 60% viewability earning $8 CPM, in-content native ads with 85% viewability earning $12 CPM, and footer banner with 25% viewability earning $4 CPM. We're considering adding a sticky sidebar ad and moving the footer banner higher up. Based on industry benchmarks and our traffic patterns of 2M monthly pageviews, what layout changes would optimize our revenue per visitor?

scenarios.title: Header Bidding Timeout Optimization
scenarios.description: Balancing header bidding timeout settings to optimize revenue vs page performance
scenarios.query: Our header bidding setup includes 12 demand partners with current 1500ms timeout. We're seeing: 85% partners respond within 1000ms averaging $7.20 CPM, 10% respond between 1000-1500ms averaging $9.80 CPM, 5% timeout completely. Our site speed decreased by 0.8 seconds affecting user experience. Should we reduce timeout to 1000ms to improve performance, and what would be the estimated revenue impact on our $50K monthly programmatic revenue?

scenarios.title: Seasonal Floor Price Strategy
scenarios.description: Developing dynamic floor pricing strategy for seasonal traffic and advertiser demand fluctuations
scenarios.query: Historical data shows our Q4 CPMs increase 40% while Q1 drops 25% compared to baseline. Our current static floor prices are: display $8, video $25, native $12. Last Q4 we had 92% fill rate but may have left money on table. This year we expect 30% traffic increase during holiday season. How should we adjust floor prices monthly from October through February to maximize revenue? Include recommendations for different content categories and device types.

scenarios.title: Mobile vs Desktop Yield Gap Analysis
scenarios.description: Analyzing and addressing revenue per visitor gap between mobile and desktop traffic
scenarios.query: Our desktop traffic (30% of total) generates $2.50 RPM while mobile (70% of total) only generates $1.20 RPM. Desktop users view 3.2 pages per session vs 1.8 for mobile. Mobile ad viewability is 15% lower and CPMs are $3 lower on average. We're considering implementing AMP, adding more mobile-optimized ad formats, or adjusting mobile floor prices. What strategy would most effectively close this $0.90 RPM gap and increase our overall monthly revenue from current $28,000?

scenarios.title: Video Ad Placement Yield Optimization
scenarios.description: Optimizing video ad placement strategy to maximize completion rates and CPMs
scenarios.query: Our video content gets 100K monthly views with current pre-roll ads at $35 CPM but only 65% completion rate. We're considering: mid-roll ads (estimated $28 CPM, 80% completion), post-roll ads ($15 CPM, 45% completion), or outstream video in articles ($22 CPM, 70% completion). Our video content averages 4 minutes length. What combination of video ad placements would maximize revenue while maintaining user experience? Include impact analysis on our current $42K monthly video revenue.

adcp-media-buy.title: AdCP Media Buy
adcp-media-buy.description: Campaign Agent walking an advertiser brief through the AdCP media buy workflow

scenarios.title: 1. Submit the Campaign Brief
scenarios.description: Hand the Campaign Agent a brief and have it confirm what it understood and what it still needs before going to market.
scenarios.query: Here is the brief for Acme Energy (brand domain acmeenergy.example), operated by Omnicom Media Group. Product: residential solar panels. Objectives: brand awareness and consideration among environmentally conscious homeowners aged 35-55. Markets: California and Texas. Channels: connected TV and online video. Budget: $750,000 USD. Flight: 1 October to 31 December 2026. Brand safety: no fossil-fuel or climate-denial content adjacency. Confirm your understanding of the brief, tell me what is missing, and outline the steps you will take to get this campaign bought.

scenarios.title: 2. Who Can We Buy From
scenarios.description: Ask which sellers the Campaign Agent can reach for this campaign and what each one supports.
scenarios.query: Which sellers can you buy from for this campaign, and what does each of them support? Name every seller explicitly so I know who answered, and if any seller did not respond, say which one rather than leaving it out.

scenarios.title: 3. Discover Inventory for the Brief
scenarios.description: Get matching products from every seller, with seller-attributed pricing, formats, and reach.
scenarios.query: Find inventory that fits the brief from every seller you can reach. For each product tell me which seller offers it, the pricing model and rate, the creative formats it supports, the estimated reach, and how it matches our audience and markets. Keep each seller's figures separate; do not blend sellers into one number.

scenarios.title: 4. Creative Requirements
scenarios.description: Check the creative formats each seller accepts for the shortlisted products against the assets we have.
scenarios.query: For the products you recommended, what creative formats does each seller accept? We have 15-second and 30-second video assets. Flag any product we could not fill with those assets, and say which seller each requirement came from.

scenarios.title: 5. Audience Signals
scenarios.description: Ask which audience or contextual signals the sellers can target against and how much coverage they offer.
scenarios.query: Which audience or contextual signals can the sellers target against to reach environmentally conscious homeowners, and what coverage and pricing does each one carry? Make clear that these figures are each seller's own data, and tell me if a seller does not offer signals at all.

scenarios.title: 6. Media Plan for Approval
scenarios.description: Assemble one media plan from the discovery results and present it for human approval.
scenarios.query: Assemble the media plan. For each seller and product give the budget, flight, pricing, expected reach, creative requirements, and risks, and show the total against the $750,000 authorization. Present it for my approval and wait. Do not book anything yet.

scenarios.title: 7. Account and Governance Setup
scenarios.description: After approval, declare the advertiser account at each seller, bind governance, and register the plan limits.
scenarios.query: The plan is approved. Declare our advertiser account with every seller for acmeenergy.example operated by Omnicom Media Group, bind the governance agent to each seller, and register the campaign plan: $750,000 USD total, flight 1 October to 31 December 2026, authorized channels connected TV, online video and streaming audio, authorized markets US with regions California and Texas, 15 percent reallocation threshold, no extra review requirement. Confirm the result per seller, and be clear that registering the plan approves nothing by itself.

scenarios.title: 8. Authorize the First Buy
scenarios.description: Check a specific intended buy against the registered plan before any money is committed.
scenarios.query: Before we spend anything, check whether a $250,000 USD buy on the first product you recommended, for the full flight and targeted to California and Texas, is within the registered plan. Report the verdict and the reason. If the answer comes back with conditions, list them and treat the buy as not approved.

scenarios.title: 9. Book the Media Buy
scenarios.description: Book the authorized buy, report the seller's confirmed figures, and close the loop with governance.
scenarios.query: Book the authorized $250,000 USD buy with that seller and product for 1 October to 31 December 2026. Report the media buy identifier, the budget the seller actually confirmed, the creative deadline, and the status. If the seller only accepted the request rather than confirming it, say so instead of implying the buy is live. Then report the outcome to the governance agent using the seller's confirmed figure, and confirm the plan's tracked spend reflects it. These are sandbox sellers, so state that no real money moved.

scenarios.title: 10. Delivery Report
scenarios.description: Get billing-grade delivery and operational status for the booked buy, with pacing against the plan.
scenarios.query: How is the booked buy delivering? Give me the billing-grade impressions and spend, and separately the operational status and creative approval state, then tell me how it is pacing against the plan. If little or nothing has delivered yet, say that plainly rather than implying delivery that has not happened.

scenarios.title: 11. Mid-Flight Change Request
scenarios.description: Ask for a reallocation and a market extension; see what the agent can check, what needs a human, and what it cannot change.
scenarios.query: Two changes: first, we want to extend the campaign into Canada with an additional $100,000 USD on the same product; second, we want to move $50,000 from the booked package to a second seller. For the Canada extension, check it against the registered plan and report the verdict and the reason. For the reallocation, tell me whether it needs human approval under our thresholds and exactly what you can and cannot do about it yourself. Do not resize or retarget anything to get it through.

scenarios.title: 12. Plan Audit Trail
scenarios.description: Read back the governance agent's record of every check, verdict, and booking on the plan.
scenarios.query: Show me the audit trail for this campaign plan as the governance agent recorded it: every authorization check and its verdict, every booking outcome, the plan's current tracked budget, and its lifecycle state. Read it back from the governance record rather than reconstructing it from our conversation.

scenarios.title: LuxeChoco RFP: Christmas Campaign

Budget €2.5M across 8 weeks Nov-Dec. They want CTV, digital video, and native across lifestyle and premium editorial content. scenarios.title: Compile Visual Media Plan

Synthesize market-by-market allocation (Germany, UK, France, Netherlands, Belgium), format mix (CTV, digital video, native), phased timeline (awareness through peak conversion), pricing summary, and audience reach projections into a structured media plan document.
